title: Finite pushforward preserves constructibility on Noetherian schemes
statement:
Let $U$ be Noetherian, let $h:V\to U$ be finite, and let $E$ be a
constructible abelian etale sheaf on $V$. Then its direct image $h_*E$ is
constructible on $U$.

proof.text: Apply the finite-stalk set-sheaf Noetherian criterion. For each integral Noetherian affine immersion $g:S\to U$, form $V_S=V\times_U S$ and $E_S=\operatorname{pr}_V^{-1}E$. The finite projection $V_S\to S$ is a base change of $h$. The specialized constructible pullback theorem gives constructibility of the underlying set sheaf of $E_S$, including finite geometric stalks.

Apply the existing generic finite-pushforward theorem over $S$ to obtain a dense open $W\subset S$ on which the underlying set sheaf of $\operatorname{pr}_{S,*}E_S$ is lisse. All its hypotheses hold: $S$ is integral, affine and Noetherian, the projection is finite, and $E_S$ has finite-stalk constructibility.

Finite exchange gives $g^{-1}h_*E\cong\operatorname{pr}_{S,*}E_S$ as abelian sheaves. The inverse-image algebraic-structures theorem identifies the underlying set sheaf of $g^{-1}h_*E$ with set inverse image of the underlying set sheaf of $h_*E$. Compose this comparison with the forgotten exchange isomorphism, pull it back along $W\to S$, and transport lissity in the reverse direction. The private Lean helper proves this transport by retaining the trivializing cover and transporting finite stalks along a bijection. Thus every test in the Noetherian criterion is satisfied; its conclusion proves the original theorem.
